35	The Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association ran a skimming station at Ostrey Hollow, seven miles up
36	the valley from its creamery at Larrow Green. For about a quarter century the milk delivered at that station
37	tested lower in butterfat than milk delivered elsewhere, and the patrons were paid less accordingly. Three
38	explanations circulated: the land (wet/bog hay thinning the cream), the patrons (watering their cans), and
39	the tester (Ansel Keddie stealing cream). All three were wrong. The station's milk-test pipettes delivered
40	16.72 c.c. against a 17.6 c.c. mark — 95 percent, one part in twenty short — so every test read 95 percent
41	of the truth. The shortfall (76,000 lb of butterfat, ~$19,000) was entered year by year in the Association's
42	own ledgers as "station gain." The glass was condemned by the state inspector in June 1923; Keddie was
